title: U.S. House · Oregon's 1st District
area: Northwest Oregon, including Washington County suburbs of Portland (Hillsboro, Beaverton area), and the north Oregon coast (Astoria, Tillamook, Lincoln City).

context.text: Incumbent Suzanne Bonamici defeated Jamil Ahmad 86.6%-12.8% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Barbara Kahl defeated John Verbeek 71.5%-27.4% in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Suzanne Bonamici

positions.summary: Supports universal background checks, a ban on magazines holding more than ten rounds, and reinstating the assault weapons ban, per her official issues page.
positions.quote: I have consistently supported bipartisan legislation to establish universal background checks, which would help stop criminals from getting weapons they are not legally allowed to purchase.

positions.summary: Supports universal health care and describes working to expand coverage as a member of the Medicare for All Caucus; also says the ACA's protections and subsidies must be maintained.
positions.quote: I support universal health care and as a member of the Medicare for All Caucus I will continue to work to expand coverage and make health care more affordable for all.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to Americans' right to choose their own health care and will keep advocating for the Women's Health Protection Act.
positions.quote: As a member of the Congressional Pro-Choice Caucus, I am committed to working for reproductive equity and the right of Oregonians and Americans to choose their own healthcare and method of family planning.

positions.summary: Describes the 2020 House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis action plan she served on as aimed at accelerating the transition to a 100 percent clean energy economy and net-zero emissions by mid-century.
positions.quote: We focused on meeting the needs of frontline communities, accelerating our transition to a 100 percent clean energy economy, and creating good-paying jobs.

positions.summary: In a February 2026 statement on the Supreme Court tariffs ruling, criticized President Trump's tariff policies as raising costs and said Congress, not the President, sets tariffs.
positions.quote: Tariffs are taxes, and Donald Trump’s chaotic tariff policies have been raising costs and causing economic uncertainty.

positions.summary: In July 2026 said she will fight against funding for immigration enforcement and introduced the Daycare Not Detentions Act to redirect $70 billion from ICE and CBP to child care programs.
positions.quote: I will continue doing all I can to fight against funding for dangerous immigration enforcement and advocate for our nation’s children and a brighter future.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Subcommittee on Environment; Subcommittee on Investigations and Oversight) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce.

candidates.researchNotes: Bonamici has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in recent cycles and her campaign site's issues page was not reachable; her House committee lists issue pages for Child Care, Civil Rights, Climate Action, Education, Health Care, Housing and other topics but their text content was not accessible in this pass.

candidates.name: Barbara Kahl

priorities.text: Fiscal discipline: cutting federal spending and redundant offices, removing ineligible recipients from benefit programs, and requiring agencies to justify funding or lose it.

Education: revising federal K-12 policy to focus on core academics (math, reading, writing, civics, history, science), restoring PE/music/art for grades K-6, and strengthening special-education support under IDEA.
Government accountability: strict budget discrepancy standards, year-end account closing, public spending reports, and routine forensic financial audits.

positions.summary: Says she supports expanding land and timber use for housing supply, workforce training in the trades, cutting permitting time and costs, and a 'buildable homes' package.
positions.quote: Housing: expanding land/timber use for supply, trades workforce training, cutting permitting time and costs, a "buildable homes" package

positions.summary: Says she will champion federal school choice legislation that lets families direct their child's education dollars to the school or program of their choice.
positions.quote: champion federal school choice legislation that empowers Oregon families — regardless of income or zip code — to direct their child’s education dollars toward the school, curriculum, or program that fits how their child actually learns

statements.quote: Supporting local law enforcement with funding and accountability — safe streets, real trust.
statements.context: On her campaign website, Public Safety platform item

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from her campaign website (home and About pages). No Ballotpedia or newsroom questionnaire answers on other guide issues were found. Kahl's campaign website could not be loaded, so her biography relies on her Ballotpedia profile and Candidate Connection survey, which are self-described.
